speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Prime Minister in light of the rise in fraudulent credit card transactions, whether the Government has considered encouraging more widespread wholesale insurance for banks and other credit card issuers that will permit easier write-offs for relatively smaller transaction amounts.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Credit card issuers such as banks have invested considerable resources in building fraud surveillance systems and controls to combat card fraud.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These systems have been enhanced over the years in response to changing technologies and methods used by the fraudsters.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Today, major banks share fraud trends with one another, enabling them to continually refine fraud rules to tackle the latest fraud techniques.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Customers should keep their cards safe and immediately report to their issuing banks if they lose their cards.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For online payments, customers should not disclose credit card details or One-Time PIN, or OTP, to anyone, and should practise strong cyber hygiene such as by regularly updating the security patches and anti-malware software on their devices.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: I find myself repeating this in Parliament and reminding people: practise good cyber hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We will continue to monitor the fraud situation and ensure that banks do their part to provide their customers with clear steps to take in order to protect themselves from such losses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I have just one supplementary question for which some motivational context behind the original question, I think, would be useful.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I mentioned just now, I keep reminding people to practise cyber hygiene, but that is by no means the only thing that we do.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I mentioned, there is a system that strikes a balance between the liability on the banks as well as on the part of consumers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As I mentioned in my reply, it is also being reviewed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I know we are all plagued by cyber crimes and scams.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Every day, we open our emails, we see some of them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, we will continue to be there and we will continue to have to strike a balance – educating but at the same time protecting consumers, but also to be fair to banks and the industry.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is something that is evolving and we will continue to work on it.
